name: Methoxydienone (Methoxy / 18-methyl)
lead: Methoxydienone, also called methoxygonadiene or 'methoxy', is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid and progestogen of the 19-nortestosterone group, related to the progestin levonorgestrel. It was never marketed as a medicine; it has been sold online as a 'designer steroid' ingredient in supplements aimed at people who want to build muscle.[1][2]

Lifters who seek it are interested in its anabolic activity, since more muscle and strength is the route to a larger, more muscular physique. Wikipedia reports that when injected it is described as a potent anabolic agent, with animal-derived anabolic-to-androgenic ratios of about 54:27 relative to testosterone propionate; no data exist on oral activity in humans.[1]

The compound was synthesised by chemist Herchel Smith and colleagues in the 1960s and 1970s during work on progestins for oral contraceptives.[1] No human trial of it has been published, and the main published human-related literature is a 2022 forensic case report.[2]

chain: Claimed gain in muscle mass and strength
angle.text: It is used for the same reason as other anabolic steroids: to add muscle mass and strength. Its anabolic effect in people has not been measured in trials, so what is known comes from animal-derived ratios and user claims.

paras: Methoxydienone has a ketone at carbon 17 and, unlike many oral anabolic steroids, is not 17alpha-alkylated.[1] It is described chemically as the 3-methyl ether of 18-methyl-19-nor-delta-2,5(10)-epiandrosterone.[1] It acts as an agonist of the androgen receptor and the progesterone receptor.[1]
Relative to testosterone propionate, an anabolic-to-androgenic ratio of about 54:27 is given for injected use, and relative to nandrolone about 90:625; oral activity in humans is unknown.[1]

The compound came out of Herchel Smith's progestin research in the 1960s and 1970s.[1] It later appeared as an ingredient in online supplements, which a 2015 review in Andrology covered among over-the-counter 'designer steroid' products.[1]

A 2022 forensic case report in Drug Testing and Analysis described a urine sample containing a putative 18-methyl-19-nortestosterone metabolite; supplements in the person's possession were found by mass spectrometry to contain methoxydienone.[2] The report is relevant to athletes subject to doping control, since 18-methyl steroids can be detected as a metabolite.

timeline.event: Herchel Smith and colleagues synthesise methoxydienone during progestin research.[1]
Andrology review covers designer steroids in over-the-counter supplements.[1]
Forensic case report links a urine finding to supplements containing methoxydienone.[2]

card.summary: A nandrolone-family designer steroid from contraceptive research that surfaced in supplements; no human trials exist.
card.note: Never approved; a forensic case shows it can cause positive doping results.

quick.overview:
Methoxydienone is a 19-nortestosterone steroid synthesised in the 1960s and 70s during progestin research. It was never a medicine, and appeared later in online supplements.

No clinical studies have examined it in people.
quick.mechanism: It is an anabolic-androgenic steroid and progestogen; animal-derived ratios reported on Wikipedia suggest anabolic activity when injected. Oral activity in humans has not been characterised.
quick.risks: No safety data in humans are published. A 2022 case report tied a supplement containing it to a detected 18-methyl steroid metabolite in a forensic urine sample, relevant for drug testing.
